subject: ENG
label: Grade 11 Humanities
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 11 Humanities English, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 5 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Prose and poetry from world writers
modules.outcome: analyse theme and voice in two texts
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Prose and poetry from world writers', taught in a way that is with exam-style questions and written reasoning. The target is clear: analyse theme and voice in two texts. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Prose and poetry from world writers' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: analyse theme and voice in two texts, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Read twice: first for the main idea, then for detail. Underline the lines that answer each question and reply in full sentences using words from the text. For poems find the rhyme, the picture and the feeling. Method: Model run for 'Prose and poetry from world writers'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Analyse theme and voice in two texts: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Prose and poetry from world writers), and at which Bloom level is it?
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 5 (Speaking and listening) run?
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A timed paper and an error log. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
